label: Rises after rare a1->S2, falls after rare a2->S1, and tracks belief S1 is good.
short_terms: (phase == D2) * (state - action) + (phase == D1) * (prev_state - prev_action) ;; belief_lo ;; (phase != D1) * (prev_reward == 0)
terms: (phase == D2) * (state - action) ;; belief_lo ;; (prev_state - prev_action) ;; (phase != D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase != D1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase == D1)*(prev_reward==0)
explanation: Raw reset gate r46. Timing dominates (high at D2, low at GO, declining over the episode). Beyond timing, the biggest driver is a signed rare-transition code at D2: a1 reaching S2 raises it strongly (+0.19 residual), a2 reaching S1 lowers it (-0.22); common transitions are near zero. The same signed (state - action) code from the previous trial carries over to the next trial at a smaller weight, and the ideal observer belief log-odds that S1 is good adds a graded offset (higher when S1 is believed good) at every phase. Reward of this trial (future) adds nothing. The free fit adds that unrewarded previous trials (and the trial before) raise it at GO/D2, and a small a1-vs-a2 offset by phase, taking dev R^2 from 0.68 to 0.78.

issues: The parts that hold up: on test, the D2 (state - action) term alone gives 0.409 and belief_lo alone gives 0.371. Together they give 0.621, and adding (prev_state - prev_action) gives 0.665. At D2 the profile shows a1->S2 at +0.195 and a2->S1 at -0.223, with common transitions near 0. So the rare-transition sign and the belief claims are correct.

The carry-over term is mis-specified. Restricting (prev_state - prev_action) to D1 scores better than the all-phase version (0.690 vs 0.665 test). The profile agrees: the previous rare code is strong at D1 (a1 S2 +0.14, a2 S1 -0.11) but at GO and D2 it mostly gives way to a reward effect (e.g. GO after a1 S2 r +0.01 vs a1 S2 u +0.118).

There is a large systematic error class the short form leaves out: an unrewarded previous trial raises the gate at GO and D2. In misses, the worst-fit dev windows are runs of unrewarded trials where GO is under-predicted by about 0.2 (e.g. actual 0.39 vs predicted 0.20 or 0.13). The top under-predicted cells are GO after a1 S1 u (+0.077), D2 after a2 S1 u (+0.071), D2 after a2 S2 u (+0.059) and D2 after a1 S1 u (+0.058). The explanation mentions this only as a free-fit extra, and the label leaves it out entirely.
The label leaves out reward and does not say when the rise and fall happen (at D2, and again at the next D1), so a reader of the label could not predict the GO-phase level.

A better short form that passes --short adds the unrewarded term: test R^2 0.7155, against 0.665 for the recorded form and an observed-only ceiling of 0.86. Its remaining errors are smaller, at most about 0.076 per cell, with D1 after a2 S1 u under-predicted.
